newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. says conditions not ripe for Iraq plan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says conditions not ripe for Iraq plan.

text.p: The United Nations is not yet satisfied that minimum conditions exist in northern Iraq for the start of an "oil-for-food" plan, U.N. Under Secrtetary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan said on Wednesday.
He was referring to the deal signed in May for the sale of $2 billion worth of Iraqi oil over six months to buy badly needed food, medicine and other humanitarian goods.

Speaking to reporters after briefing the Security Council in private, he said Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali would like to be able to report to the council as soon as possible that conditions were ripe for putting the plan into operation.
"As I said to the Security Council...we are not looking for perfect conditions in which to operate," he said.
"But we will insist on certain minimum conditions to be established on the ground before we can consider starting this whole process. We are not yet satisifed that we are there," he added.

He referred particularly to the need for freedom of movement of U.N. staff in the largely Kurdish-inhabited north of the country, which Iraqi troops entered at the end of August for the first time since the end of the 1991 Gulf War. Another issue was Iraq's wish for new local U.N. staff to be recruited, Gharekhan added.
